ministry_ne: कानून, न्याय तथा संसदीय मामिला मन्त्रालय
summary:
The main purpose of the Mediation (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083 or Mediation (Second Amendment) Act, 2083 is to increase public access to justice by resolving disputes through quick and simple procedures via mediation, expand mediation work to the provincial and local levels in line with Nepal's federal structure, and make contemporary amendments to the Act enacted in the year 2068 (Objective and Reasons, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

Communities can establish community mediation centres at the local level with the support and collaboration of the concerned local level to make community mediation work systematic and effective (Objective and Reasons, Page 1; Section 27, Page 10). If a Judicial Committee has formed a ward-level mediation centre, the operation of the community mediation centre may be integrated and coordinated (Section 27, Page 10). The establishment and operation of community mediation centres shall be as determined by local level law (Section 27, Page 10). The concerned local level shall provide identity cards to mediators included in the mediator group (Section 25, Page 9). The written record of dispute resolution outcomes through community-based mediation must be sent for record-keeping to the local level mediation centre or ward committee office, and that office must keep the record secure (Section 26, Page 9; Section 26, Page 10). The local level may audit and inspect the accounts of the community mediation centre fund at any time, and the operation of the fund shall be governed by local level law (Section 27, Page 10). The Village Executive or Municipal Executive may provide necessary technical services to community-based mediators and community mediation centres (Section 28, Page 11). When a case is received from an adjudicating body for mediation at the local level, the Judicial Committee of the local level must resolve the dispute through mediation within 3 months from receipt and inform the adjudicating body, or return the case file and documents with an explanation if mediation cannot be achieved within that period (Section 32, Page 13). A Provincial Mediation Coordination Committee shall be established in each province for provincial-level coordination, monitoring, evaluation, and facilitation (Section 22, Page 6). This committee is responsible for conducting programs, monitoring mediation work, coordinating among institutions, and submitting an annual report containing details of mediation work in the province to the Council by the 15th of Bhadra every year (Section 22, Page 7). At the federal level, the Council shall make recommendations to the relevant ministry of the Government of Nepal regarding support to be provided by provincial and local levels to promote mediation (Section 20, Page 5). In addition, the Council must obtain approval from the Government of Nepal, Ministry of Finance before receiving foreign funds into the Mediation Fund (Section 24, Page 9).

Organized institutions registered under prevailing law operating mediation services must perform dispute resolution in accordance with their procedures approved by the Council (Section 10, Page 2; Section 18, Page 4). When a mediation deed or settlement agreement is executed for dispute resolution under this Act, the concerned parties must execute that mediation deed or settlement document within 45 days from the date of its execution (Section 30, Subsection 1, Page 11). A party wishing to enforce a foreign mediation deed in Nepal must file an application with the concerned district court within 90 days from the date the mediation deed was prepared (Section 31, Page 12). The applicant must attach to the application the original or certified copy of the mediation deed and, if it is not in the Nepali language, a certified official translation in Nepali (Section 31, Page 12). The Provincial Mediation Coordination Committee must prepare an annual report including details of mediation work in the province and submit it to the Council by the 15th of Bhadra every year (Section 22, Page 7). The local level Judicial Committee must resolve a referred case through mediation within 3 months from receipt and inform the adjudicating body (Section 32, Page 13).

Mediator certificates shall be issued by the Council upon receiving the prescribed fee (Section 14, Page 3). The certificate shall remain valid for 5 years from the date of issue and must be renewed by paying the prescribed renewal fee (Section 14, Page 3). The renewal of certificates shall be managed by the Council Secretariat and the Mediation Monitoring Committee (Section 14, Page 3). The Council shall cancel a mediator certificate following the prescribed procedure if the mediator acts contrary to clause (d), (e), (f), or (g) of Section 12, loses qualification under Section 22, or engages in fraudulent or forged acts during work (Section 14, Page 3). Regarding qualifications, if a person with a bachelor's degree is not available for mediation at the local level, a person who has passed at least secondary education or equivalent qualification may work as a mediator (Section 15, Page 4). A district judge designated by the Chief Justice from among district judges working in a district court with 5 or more judges to act as a mediator must have taken basic mediation training (Section 7, Page 2). Mediators may conduct mediation discussions and facilitation through video conference complying with standards determined by the Council (Section 29, Page 11).

A Commercial Sector Mediation Promotion Committee shall be established to resolve commercial disputes through mediation and run programs to promote commercial mediation, comprising a Council member designated by the Chairperson as Coordinator, the President of Nepal Bankers Association, President of FNCCI, President of Nepal Chamber of Commerce, President of CNI, two members nominated by the Council representing commercial associations/federations in
title: Mediation (Second Amendment) Bill, 2083
